question.text: For a Cat III AIF, on T-day (inception) of an options contract, Total Exposure equals:

answer.text: Option strike price multiplied by lot size
Option premium per unit multiplied by lot size only (ignoring number of lots)
Option premium paid - where the per-unit premium is multiplied by lot-size and number of lots to arrive at total premium paid

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook (pp. 321, 323-324), option exposure on T-day equals the option premium paid for entering into the option contract. Where premium is quoted per unit, total premium paid is computed as premium x lot-size x lots. From T+1 onwards the option is repriced via mark-to-market. Example 12.12 applies this premium-based exposure for offsetting in the leverage calculation. The Trap: Strike x lot-size overstates exposure; "zero until exercise" is wrong; premium x lot-size without including the number of lots ignores scale. Note: SEBI T-day exposure is premium-based, not underlying-notional-based. Reasoning that relies on deep-OTM "notional leverage" can be misleading because the regulatory measure here is the premium paid.
